bib.title: ELECTRA: Pre-training Text Encoders as Discriminators Rather than Generators

question: Can a pre-training task defined over all input tokens (replaced token detection) train text encoders with less compute than masked language modeling?
hypothesis: Learning from all input tokens rather than only the ~15% masked ones makes pre-training more compute-efficient and yields better downstream accuracy.
contributions: Replaced token detection pre-training task with a small jointly trained MLM generator
Ablations on weight sharing, generator size and training algorithms
Compute-matched comparisons from Small (1 GPU) to Large against BERT, RoBERTa, XLNet, ALBERT
Efficiency analysis separating the all-token loss from the [MASK] mismatch

method.summary: A small masked-LM generator fills masked positions with samples; the ELECTRA discriminator (a Transformer encoder) labels every token as original or replaced. Both are trained jointly with L_MLM + lambda*L_Disc; the generator is discarded afterwards and the discriminator is fine-tuned on GLUE and SQuAD.
method.task: self-supervised pre-training of text encoders (replaced token detection), evaluated by fine-tuning on GLUE and SQuAD

datasets.name: Wikipedia + BooksCorpus (BERT data)
datasets.preprocessing: dynamic token masking; no next-sentence prediction

datasets.name: XLNet pre-training data
datasets.source: Wikipedia, BooksCorpus, ClueWeb, CommonCrawl, Gigaword; used for ELECTRA-Large and the ++ models

datasets.name: GLUE
datasets.size: train sizes: CoLA 8.5k, SST 67k, MRPC 3.7k, STS 5.8k, QQP 364k, MNLI 393k, QNLI 108k, RTE 2.5k
datasets.split: dev set unless stated; test set for Tables 3 and 8

datasets.name: SQuAD 1.1 and 2.0
datasets.split: dev; SQuAD 2.0 test for one submission

other.note: same hyperparameters as the matching ELECTRA size

models.name: ELMo, GPT, RoBERTa, XLNet, ALBERT, SpanBERT

training.objective: min over theta_G, theta_D of sum_x L_MLM(x,theta_G) + lambda*L_Disc(x,theta_D); lambda=50; discriminator loss not back-propagated to generator; expectations approximated with a single sample
training.steps: ELECTRA 1M Small, 766K Base, 400K Large (BERT 1.45M/1M/464K); also Large 1.75M; ++ models 4e6
training.seq_len: 128 for Small; 512 for Small++; others not stated (BERT-Base hyperparameters)
training.hardware: Small: 1 V100 GPU; Base: 16 TPUv3s (Table 1); ELMo 3 GTX 1080; GPT 8 P6000
training.compute: Small 1.4e18 train FLOPs; Base 6.4e19; Large-400K 7.1e20; Large-1.75M 3.1e21
training.wall_clock: Small 4d on 1 V100; Base 4d on 16 TPUv3s
training.seeds: median of 10 fine-tuning runs from the same pre-trained checkpoint

other.weight_sharing: embeddings (token and positional) tied between generator and discriminator; generator input/output embeddings tied
other.hp_search: lr for Base and Small from [1e-4,2e-4,3e-4,5e-4]; lambda from [1,10,20,50,100]
other.finetune: GLUE lr 3e-4 Small, 1e-4 Base, 5e-5 Large; layerwise LR decay 0.8 Base/Small, 0.9 Large; linear decay; warmup fraction 0.1; batch 32; weight decay 0; epochs 10 RTE/STS, 2 SQuAD, 3 others; dropout 0.1
other.small_model_derivation: from BERT-Base: seq len 512->128, batch 256->128, hidden 768->256, embeddings 768->128
other.test_tricks: intermediate MNLI training for RTE/STS, WNLI antecedent scoring, ensemble best 10 of 30 seeds; SQuAD 2.0 test: best dev of 20 models

inference.samples: median of 10 fine-tuning runs per result

metrics.name: GLUE score
metrics.definition: average over tasks; Spearman for STS, Matthews for CoLA, accuracy for the rest

metrics.name: Train FLOPs
metrics.definition: counted with TensorFlow profiler, checked by hand; backward pass = forward; matmul = 2mn

eval.protocol: Median of 10 fine-tuning runs from one checkpoint, dev set unless stated; comparisons at matched FLOPs.

availability.weights: to be released at same URL

limits: Own BERT-Large baseline scores notably worse than RoBERTa-100K, so it may need more tuning or the RoBERTa data; XLNet-data vs RoBERTa-data comparison is not fully direct.
GLUE test comparisons are less apples-to-apples because of ensembling and task tricks.
Training times are for different hardware and sometimes unoptimised code.
Explanation of parameter efficiency is speculative; authors say more analysis is needed.
English only; FLOPs ignore hardware effects such as ALBERT's communication savings.
Authors did not search per-task hyperparameters and expect small gains from doing so.
